{{Short description|Czech mathematician}}
'''Thomas J. Jech''' ({{langx|cs|Tomáš Jech}}, {{IPA|cs|ˈtomaːʃ ˈjɛx|pron}}; born 29 January 1944 in [[Prague]]) is a [[mathematician]] specializing in [[set theory]] who was at [[Penn State]] for more than 25 years.

==Life==
He was educated at [[Charles University]] (his advisor was [[Petr Vopěnka]]) and from 2000 is at the [http://www.math.cas.cz/ Institute of Mathematics] of the [[Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic]].

==Work==
Jech's research also includes [[mathematical logic]], [[algebra]], [[analysis]], [[topology]], and [[measure theory]].

Jech gave the first published proof of the consistency of the existence of a [[Suslin's problem|Suslin line]].
With [[Karel Prikry]], he introduced the notion of [[precipitous ideal]].<ref name="Precipitous">{{cite journal | last=Jech | first=Thomas | last2=Prikry | first2=Karel | title=On ideals of sets and the power set operation | journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] | volume=82 | issue=4 | date=1976 | issn=0273-0979 | doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1976-14121-3 | doi-access=free | pages=593–595 | url=https://www.ams.org/bull/1976-82-04/S0002-9904-1976-14121-3/S0002-9904-1976-14121-3.pdf | access-date=2025-03-04}}</ref> He gave several models where the [[axiom of choice]] failed, for example one with ω<sub>1</sub> [[measurable cardinal|measurable]]. The concept of a [[Jech–Kunen tree]] is named after him and [[Kenneth Kunen]].
